purpose: Define the admissible agent-submission band and deterministic rejection responses. This is an input-validation specification; it does not implement a validator.

boundary.machine_validation: JSON syntax, envelope shape, current-index structural fields and supplied progression identity/prefix predicates only.
boundary.semantic_validation: None. Do not evaluate meaning, quality, correctness, usefulness, reasoning depth, source interpretation, or whether the task is substantively complete.
boundary.semantic_fields: A field named semantic_completion or final_output does not authorize semantic evaluation; only explicitly declared structural type/presence predicates apply.
boundary.termination: Both accepted and rejected submissions are successfully processed validation outcomes. Rejection is not a process crash, acceptance or advancement. Infrastructure failures remain explicit execution failures.

inputs.payload_text: Complete candidate JSON text supplied as a value by the caller, regardless of its origin.
inputs.source_identity: Opaque submission/context identity supplied by the caller; it identifies a logical validation context, not an input location.
inputs.state_snapshot: Current accepted prefix and expected index supplied as values; this procedure neither retrieves nor persists state.
inputs.procedure: Current procedure object and structural definitions supplied as values.
inputs.bound_operation: Supplied operator/mode when the structural output schema depends on it.

types.nonempty_string: JSON string with at least one non-whitespace character
types.conditional: Evaluate only its declared structural applicability rule; never guess from semantic prose

error.pointer: RFC 6901 pointer to failing input; empty string for root or parse failure
error.observed: Type/shape summary, not an echo of the full submission

shared_definitions.preserved_prefix: Compare parsed JSON values using the prefix representation and equality/hash convention supplied with the validation context. Formatting-only differences are not substantive prefix changes.

predicates.check: payload_text parses as exactly one JSON value without Markdown fences, prose or trailing non-whitespace text
supplied candidate identity matches the expected logical context identity supplied by the caller
candidate adds exactly one entry at the supplied expected index and stays within the supplied progression protocol
previously accepted prefix matches the supplied accepted-prefix value/hash
current index exists uniquely in current procedure; resolve definition_ref using current index_contract_reference_rules
predicates.classification: execution failure if canonical configuration is absent or contradictory; do not blame agent input

predicates.check: new scratchpad satisfies the current resolved output.scratchpad_contract structural requirements
conditional/operator-specific output fields satisfy their supplied structural schema, when applicable

non_predicates: Whether a string is true or a good answer
Whether framing is deep or original
Whether an opcode was semantically executed
Whether the final deliverable actually satisfies the user
Whether cited evidence supports a substantive claim
accepted_band.nonempty_rule: Only enforce nonempty content where explicitly specified; empty arrays/objects are not automatically invalid for every field.
accepted_band.unknown_fields: Do not reject additional substantive scratchpad fields unless an exact-key rule explicitly prohibits them; outer wrapper remains exact-key.
accepted_band.missing_schema: If a required structural rule cannot be resolved unambiguously, terminate with an explicit configuration failure instead of inventing a schema or treating the agent submission as invalid.

per_index_binding.iteration: For each current index_contracts record, identify by index/contract_id rather than a saved positional pointer table.
per_index_binding.resolve: Resolve its current definition_ref recursively with exact conflict/cycle checks.
per_index_binding.structural_source: Resolved output.scratchpad_contract supplies required field names, types, nested required_fields, exact wrapper/length requirements and explicit coverage requirements.
per_index_binding.criteria_exclusion: Never execute semantic_completion.stage_criteria or shared semantic criteria as acceptance predicates.
per_index_binding.preparation: Use the declared five-part preparation shape and its explicitly defined field/type requirements.
per_index_binding.framing: Use the declared reference-A/reference-B/result output shape. Supplied operator and mode determine only the applicable output-field schema, not a semantic verdict.
per_index_binding.reconciliation: Check declared coverage arrays and field structures; do not determine whether reconciliation is substantively adequate.
per_index_binding.final: Check the final field types and any conditional output-data structures declared by the supplied contract. Structural acceptance does not establish semantic success or actual delivery.
per_index_binding.unsupported_rule_language: Unsupported or ambiguous schema clauses are configuration failures, not implied authorization for model judgment.

error_catalog.INVALID_JSON: Invalid JSON. Submit one JSON array without Markdown fences or surrounding text.
error_catalog.INVALID_ROOT: Invalid root type. Expected one JSON array.
error_catalog.INVALID_WRAPPER: Invalid entry wrapper. Expected exactly one nonempty scratchpad object.
error_catalog.SOURCE_MISMATCH: Submission identity does not match the supplied validation context.
error_catalog.OUT_OF_SEQUENCE: Invalid entry count or index. Submit only the requested next entry.
error_catalog.PREFIX_CHANGED: Previously accepted entries were changed. Preserve the accepted prefix.
error_catalog.INVALID_FIELD: Missing or invalid field. Correct the field identified by pointer and expected type.
error_catalog.INVALID_OPERATION_OUTPUT: Output does not match the structural fields required by the supplied operation or mode.
error_catalog.CONTRACT_UNAVAILABLE: Validation configuration unavailable or inconsistent. No acceptance decision was made.
error_catalog.EXECUTION_UNAVAILABLE: Required input, state or configuration values were not supplied. No acceptance decision was made.

procedure.reason: Bind the supplied candidate and validation context; do not retrieve input or rely on an agent acceptance claim.

procedure.on_invalid: Return rejected result with a specific error; terminate successfully.
procedure.reason: Malformed envelopes are outside the admissible band regardless of meaning.

procedure.on_invalid: Return rejected result without advancement; terminate successfully.
procedure.reason: A valid JSON value is not sufficient if it edits accepted history or skips the requested entry.

procedure.on_failure: Return failed/not_evaluated configuration result; no advancement.
procedure.reason: Input shape follows the current supplied contract rather than a duplicated fixed list of schemas.

procedure.on_invalid: Return rejected result with pointer/type errors; terminate successfully.
procedure.reason: Only declared mechanical predicates narrow acceptance. Semantic claims are not judged.
Return structural acceptance as a value. The caller decides whether a separately configured state-management operation consumes it.

rejected.errors: One or more specific error records; preserve accepted state.

execution_failure.errors: Explicit source/state/configuration failure; do not call this a semantic rejection.

examples.case: Valid JSON object instead of array
Correct structure with a factually wrong or low-quality answer

environment_boundary.scope: Pure procedure over supplied in-memory values; independent of storage, transport, hosting service, user interface and delivery destination.
environment_boundary.caller_responsibility: A separately configured adapter obtains inputs and receives results. This procedure does not choose, describe or access those locations.
environment_boundary.input_rule: Inputs are values passed to this procedure; names and references identify logical data, not physical sources.
environment_boundary.output_rule: Return result values to the caller. EMIT means returning/serializing a value; it does not mean writing a file, posting a comment or sending a message.
environment_boundary.references: RFC 6901 references resolve within the supplied procedure object only, without external retrieval.
environment_boundary.configuration: Concrete input/output bindings and adapter implementations belong in a separate configuration document.
